title: Experts disagree on turn-end backstop
context:
Chief architect: Ruled by the chief: all three criteria stand. The boundary the tester asks for is settled deterministically, with no clock: if either the payload or the stage ledger says a stage agent is running, defer; the ledger wins when the payload is empty. A clean hand-off between stages (the last stage ended with its artifact, the next not yet started, the change still open) writes no failed verify and no red verdict. A change that is really half done (a stage ended without its artifact, or a stage open with no agent running) is still judged, receipted and shown red.

Target: turn-end backstop
- qa-engineer: Given a stage_start row and a Stop payload whose background_tasks lists a running stage agent, when the turn ends, then no stage_end, verify, receipt.json, cost.json seal or HUD verdict file is written for the change (proof: integration test replaying the recorded timeline).
- qa-engineer: Negative case: given stage N has ended and stage N+1 has not started (an orchestrator turn end between stages), when the turn ends, then no failed verify is written and the HUD verdict stays non-red.
- qa-engineer: Boundary: the race where the stage agent is running but the Stop payload carries an empty or missing background_tasks array must have its own criterion stating which signal wins (ledger running stage vs payload), so the test is deterministic and not clock-timed.
